Ridgeline Eight Win Final by a Bow Ball

Sam Whitaker · Sunday 18 October 2026

It came down to the last stroke… and then to a photograph. The Ridgeline University first eight won the autumn final on Saturday by roughly the length of a bow ball, after a race in which they trailed for all but the final ten metres.

Riverside led from the start, pushing out to a half-length lead at the first bridge, and it looked for a long time as though their heavier crew would hold on. Ridgeline’s cox, Mia Larsen, called for a push with three hundred metres to go—her third of the race—and the gap finally began to close.

“I honestly didn’t know if we’d got it,” said stroke Oliver Grant, who was slumped over his oar when the result was announced. “We just kept going, because there wasn’t anything else to do.” The judges took nearly four minutes to review the finish camera.

Result: 1. Ridgeline 5:41.2   2. Riverside 5:41.3   3. Northgate 5:49.8

The win is Ridgeline’s first in the event since 2019, and it comes after a season in which the club lost three senior rowers to graduation. Head coach Elena Duarte credited the younger athletes, several of whom had never raced an eight before last year.

Both crews now turn to the winter head races, where they will meet again in December over a longer course. Full results for every category are posted on the club results page.
